one_liner: Google's pay-per-click ad platform for Search, Display, YouTube and Shopping campaigns.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 only. Three workflows: multi-user (end users authorize their own Ads accounts), single-user, and service account (JWT, recommended for accounts you already manage). Developer tokens (GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN) were sunset on 2026-09-09; API access level now comes from the Google Cloud project that owns the OAuth client or service account. login-customer-id is used when acting through a manager account.
access_notes: Access levels are per Cloud project. Test access is automatic but only reaches test accounts. Explorer (production, 2,880 ops/day, some services restricted) is requested via 'Apply for access' in Cloud Console with automated review. Basic (15,000 ops/day) needs brand verification. Standard (unlimited) needs a manual compliance audit (~10 business days) and Required Minimum Functionality.
api_breadth_notes: RPC reference lists ~112 services and several hundred resources; GAQL Search/SearchStream plus Mutate across campaigns, ad groups, ads, assets, audiences, conversions, billing, planning, recommendations.
mcp_notes: googleads/google-ads-mcp, documented on developers.google.com. Runs locally (stdio via pipx) or self-deployed as remote streamable-http on Cloud Run with OAuth. Read tools (list_accessible_customers, search, get_resource_metadata) plus limited writes (create_asset, upload_video_asset, labels) with propose-and-confirm; no campaign/budget/bid changes.
blocker: Production accounts need Explorer/Basic/Standard approval of Cloud project
notes: Test manager/client accounts are free, need no approval, serve no ads and return empty serving metrics (max 50 per test hierarchy, deleted after 1 year inactive). Explorer is quick to get but restricts account creation/linking, user management, planning and billing services. Standard access includes permissible-use categories (ad management, reporting, research). No push/webhook mechanism documented; polling via GAQL. Older docs/configs that still require a developer token are outdated after 2026-09-09.

one_liner: Meta's API for creating, managing and reporting on Facebook and Instagram ads.
auth_notes: Facebook Login (for Business) OAuth with ads_read / ads_management scopes yields user access tokens; system user access tokens for server-to-server. Tokens sent as Graph API access tokens / Bearer.
access_notes: Marketing API access tier defaults to Limited (development, heavily rate-limited, calls hit production data). Full access needs App Review plus 500+ successful calls in 15 days with <15% error rate. Managing other people's ad accounts requires advanced access to ads_read/ads_management via App Review; Business Verification required for sensitive data.
api_breadth_notes: Graph API Marketing API: campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, insights, audiences, catalogs, signals/datasets, A/B and lift studies, ad account webhooks.
mcp_notes: Meta-hosted remote Ads MCP server at https://mcp.facebook.com/ads. Auth via OAuth (Facebook Login for Business), user access token as Bearer, or Employee-role system user token; needs ads_mcp_management plus ads_read or ads_management. Seven tool categories incl. reporting, ad creation/management, catalog, signals, help, A/B and lift tests, activity logs (read+write). Owning a Meta app is not required.
blocker: Managing others' ad accounts needs App Review advanced access
notes: One sandbox ad account per app (no payment method, ads never deliver, Insights API not supported, only via API). Ads webhooks cover 6 ad_account fields (effective_status, subscriptions, creative_fatigue, ad_recommendations, in_process_ad_objects, with_issues_ad_objects). Standard-access ads permissions suffice only for your own ad account. The /docs/marketing-api/sandbox-mode URL returned 404; sandbox details come from Meta's 2023 developer blog post.

one_liner: LinkedIn Marketing APIs for B2B ad campaigns, reporting, leads and conversions.
auth_notes: All Marketing API permissions are member (3-legged) OAuth 2.0 authorization-code scopes, e.g. r_ads, rw_ads, r_ads_reporting, rw_organization_admin. Members also need the right ad account / Page roles. Developer Portal token generator available for testing.
access_notes: Requires a LinkedIn Page and a developer app, then applying for the Advertising API under the app's Products tab. Development tier: unlimited reads, edits on up to 5 ad accounts, 1 test ad account via API. Standard tier via support ticket with demo video. Audience Insights/Media Planning restricted; Company Intelligence closed to new applicants.
api_breadth_notes: Versioned REST (monthly versions): Advertising (accounts, campaigns, creatives, reporting, boosts), Community Management, Lead Sync, Conversions, Events, Matched Audiences, plus restricted Audience Insights and Media Planning.
mcp_notes: No LinkedIn-published MCP server found; only third-party servers (PyPI/npm packages, AdKit, AdPlug, CData).
blocker: Advertising API access needs LinkedIn application approval
notes: LinkedIn reviews use cases against restricted-use rules and may decline even qualified apps. Development-tier ad accounts must be mapped to the app in the Developer Portal. Community Management dev tier: 500 calls/app/day and 100/member/day, no BATCH_GET, no social-action webhooks. 'Sandbox' here means the single test ad account allowed in Development tier, not a separate environment. Version 202601 sunsets 2027-01-15.

one_liner: All-in-one CRM, funnels and marketing automation platform for agencies and SMBs.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 Marketplace apps (agency or sub-account/location tokens, access tokens expire daily and are refreshed) for public integrations and webhooks. Private Integration Tokens (static OAuth-like bearer tokens with chosen scopes, agency or sub-account level, ~90-day rotation recommended) for internal use. Legacy v1 API keys superseded.
access_notes: Anyone can sign up for a Marketplace developer account and create sandbox App Test accounts (Enterprise-feature trial, rate-limited 25 req/10s and 10k/day, up to 6 months) to get PITs and test OAuth; docs do not state a price. Production API is on Starter ($97/mo), Unlimited ($297/mo) and Founder ($497/mo); some endpoints (Create Sub-Account, Enable SaaS) need Founder.
api_breadth_notes: Official MCP exposes 717 actions across 38 feature areas (contacts, conversations, calendars, opportunities, payments, locations, etc.).
mcp_notes: HighLevel-hosted remote LeadConnector MCP (Streamable HTTP): https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2 (Claude), /mcp/openai/v2/, /mcp/cursor/v2, /mcp/muse/v2/. Sign in with HighLevel login and pick sub-accounts; 4 meta-tools (list_locations, search_operations, describe_operation, execute_operation).
blocker: Some endpoints Founder-plan only; sandbox accounts expire
notes: Webhooks are tied to OAuth Marketplace apps, not PITs. Tokens are scoped to either an agency (company) or a sub-account (location), so toolkits must handle per-location auth; cross-sub-account switching needs bulk installation. Sandbox App Test account details came from marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/oauth/SandboxAccount.md and SandboxPIT. The hinted highlevel.stoplight.io overview page returned no content.

one_liner: Email marketing and automation platform for audiences, campaigns and reporting.
auth_notes: OAuth 2 authorization-code flow via apps registered in the account (client_id/secret, token at login.mailchimp.com/oauth2/token). API keys for own-account use, sent via HTTP Basic (any username, key as password) or as token in client libraries. Keys created on or after 2026-06-22 expire after 1 year.
access_notes: Free plan (under 250 contacts, 500 sends/mo, 1 seat, 1 audience). API keys can be generated by users with Manager role or above; the help and pricing pages tie no API restriction to a plan.
api_breadth_notes: Marketing API v3 (OpenAPI-described) covers audiences/members, campaigns, automations, reports, templates, e-commerce, landing pages, file manager and more; well over 100 operations.
mcp_notes: Intuit Mailchimp connector for Claude (account sign-in; plans/edits campaigns and saves drafts; Owner/Admin role). Separate docs-only remote MCP at https://mailchimp.com/developer/_mcp/server (no account data).
notes: Audience webhooks (subscribe, unsubscribe, profile/email changes, campaign sending) configurable via UI or API, with optional HMAC-SHA256 signing secret. Account-scoped base URLs use a data-center prefix (not confirmed on fetched pages). Free plan lacks automation flows and scheduling, so some endpoints may fail on free accounts. Mailchimp Transactional (Mandrill) is a separate product with separate keys. The Claude connector's public endpoint URL was not confirmed on an official page; its exact scope beyond campaign planning is unclear.

one_liner: Email, SMS and customer data platform for ecommerce marketing automation.
auth_notes: Private API keys (pk_ prefix) in header 'Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key <key>', with Custom/Read-only/Full scopes fixed at creation. OAuth for partner apps (required for App Marketplace listing) with resource:read/write scopes. Public 6-char company ID for client-side /client endpoints.
access_notes: Developers can create an additional free test (sandbox) Klaviyo account linked to their login; private keys created under Settings > API keys by Owner/Admin/Manager roles.
api_breadth_notes: JSON:API-style REST with dated revisions: profiles, lists, segments, events, metrics, campaigns (omnichannel), flows, templates, catalogs, reporting, webhooks and more.
mcp_notes: Klaviyo-hosted remote MCP at https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth with dynamic client registration, Owner/Admin/Manager role; read-only=true query param). Local option: uvx klaviyo-mcp-server@latest with PRIVATE_API_KEY.
notes: Webhooks API is limited to Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners (OAuth apps); app-created webhooks are owned by the app. Rate limits are per account with burst and steady windows, listed per endpoint. API key scopes cannot be edited after creation. Endpoint count not tallied this session.

one_liner: All-in-one funnel builder with email marketing, courses, memberships and online sales.
auth_notes: Public API keys sent in the X-API-Key header (only method supported). Created under Settings > MCP & API keys; max 3 keys, optional expiration, shown once. No OAuth.
access_notes: Free plan exists (no card, up to 2,000 contacts, 3 funnels). API key creation is in account settings; no fetched page states which plans include the public API. Pricing page has an 'API requests per minute' row whose per-plan values did not load.
api_breadth_notes: Fetched reference page only showed contacts and tags; MCP coverage suggests more (contact fields, newsletters, funnels, courses, products, coupons, bookings). Exact public API count not verified.
mcp_notes: systeme.io's own MCP server (docs at developer.systeme.io/docs/mcp-server) authenticated with MCP keys (max 2 active, up to 90 days); covers contacts, tags, fields, newsletters, funnels, price plans, coupons, automations, products, bookings, courses, SMS templates. Initial release; OAuth planned; ChatGPT connection in beta.
notes: Webhooks configured in Settings > Webhooks with secret key and HTTPS URL: contact created, tag added/removed, form opt-in, new sale, sale canceled; up to 12 retries. Rate-limit quota shared across all keys (429 with Retry-After). Collections use cursor pagination (startingAfter, limit). The help article 2329 on the public API returned no content. Whether the free plan includes API/webhooks is unconfirmed.

one_liner: Visual discovery platform; API v5 for pins, boards, ads, catalogs and analytics.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code (full API access) with continuous refresh tokens (60-day, refreshable indefinitely; access tokens 30 days). Client credentials grant only for your own developer account (needs 2FA, some endpoints blocked). Scopes like pins:read, boards:write, ads:read, catalogs:write.
access_notes: App must be approved for Trial access (public privacy policy, detailed description). Trial: daily per-app limits, pins/boards created are sandbox entities visible only to creator. Standard access requires an upgrade request with a demo video showing OAuth flow and live integration; no published review timeline.
api_breadth_notes: v5 covers pins, boards, sections, media, user accounts, ad accounts, campaigns, ad groups, ads, targeting, keywords, lead forms, billing, catalogs/feeds/product groups, conversions.
mcp_notes: Pinterest-announced hosted MCP at https://api.pinterest.com/mcp (OAuth 2.0 bearer; organic and Ads capabilities). Page invites 'sign up for updates', so general availability is unconfirmed; third-party sources describe it as partner-only alpha.
blocker: Standard access needs review with demo video; Trial is sandbox-limited
notes: Sandbox host api-sandbox.pinterest.com (Trial or Standard; no video pins, shopping ads, conversions or auction simulation). Only webhook-like feature is Lead Ads subscriptions (encrypted lead delivery to webhook_url), which needs Lead Ads beta access. Apps registered on/after 2026-09-14 may get 403 PINNER_DATA_ACCESS_DENIED for non-business users' boards/pins. Forum reports describe Standard upgrades stuck pending for weeks. Fetches of /docs/getting-started/set-up-app/ and /docs/getting-started/authentication-and-scopes/ returned 404.

one_liner: Meta's text-based social network; API for publishing, replies, insights and search.
auth_notes: Threads authorization window (OAuth code, valid 1 hour) exchanged for short-lived token (1h), then long-lived token (60 days, refreshable via /refresh_access_token). Uses separate Threads app ID/secret within a Meta app. Permissions: threads_basic (required) plus content_publish, delete, keyword_search, location_tagging, manage_insights, manage_mentions, manage_replies, profile_discovery, read_replies.
access_notes: Self-serve Meta app with the Threads use case; invited Threads Testers can grant permissions anytime. Other users need each permission approved through App Review and a published app; keyword search beyond own posts needs threads_keyword_search approval.
api_breadth_notes: graph.threads.net endpoints for publishing (text, image, video, carousel), media retrieval, replies and reply management, insights, profile discovery, keyword search, mentions, location search, deletion, oEmbed, webhooks; roughly 20-40 operations.
mcp_notes: No Meta-published Threads MCP found; several community servers (meta-threads-mcp on PyPI, pegasusheavy/threads-mcp, etc.). Meta's official Ads MCP does not cover Threads organic posting.
blocker: Non-tester users require Meta App Review per permission
notes: Rate limits: 250 posts and 1,000 replies per 24h, 100 deletions/24h, call budget scales with impressions. Webhook topics: replies, delete, mentions, publish. Docs conflict: the use-case page says webhooks need a published app but not App Review, while the webhooks page says advanced access via App Review (and business verification) is required to receive notifications. Media must be on a public URL at publish time. No separate sandbox; testing uses tester accounts on real Threads profiles.

one_liner: Twilio's transactional email API and email marketing campaigns platform.
auth_notes: API keys sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. Key types: Full Access, Custom Access (per-scope permissions, editable later), Billing Access; up to 100 keys; first key created in UI. Parent accounts can act for subusers via on-behalf-of header. No OAuth flow for third-party apps documented.
access_notes: Free Email API and Marketing Campaigns plans retired May 2025. New accounts get a one-time 60-day trial (100 emails/day, 100 contacts) in which API keys work; after it, sending stops until upgrading to Essentials ($19.95/mo+), Pro ($89.95/mo+) or Premier.
api_breadth_notes: Official OpenAPI repo has 46 v3 spec files: Mail Send, templates, Marketing Campaigns (contacts, lists, segments, single sends, designs, stats), suppressions, stats, subusers, teammates, IPs, domain/link branding, webhooks, email validation, SSO, etc.
mcp_notes: No Twilio-published SendGrid MCP server found; Twilio blog has a build-your-own tutorial and there are community servers (neschadin, deyikong, Garoth).
blocker: No free plan; 60-day trial then paid plan
notes: Event Webhook (delivery, engagement, account-status events; signed webhook and OAuth 2.0 options for securing the receiver) with 1 webhook on trial, 2 on Essentials, 5 on Pro/Premier; Inbound Parse also exists. Mail Send sandbox_mode validates requests without delivering or consuming credits. Email Address Validation and billing endpoints are excluded from Full Access keys. Pricing data from twilio.com/en-us/products/email-api/pricing; sendgrid.com/pricing redirects.
